He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis Tigers]] and [[TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball|TCU Horned Frogs]]. ==Early life and high school career== Baugh attended Cane Ridge High School for two seasons before transferring to Lincoln Academy. For his senior season, he joined Tennessee Prep Academy.{{cite news|first=Mark|last=Giannotto|title=Antavion Collum, Damion Baugh put Tennessee Prep on the college basketball recruiting map|url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/college/memphis-tigers/basketball/2018/07/23/antavion-collum-damion-baugh-tennessee-prep-college-basketball-recruiting-map-penny-hardaway/818616002/|work=[[Memphis Commercial Appeal]]|date=July 23, 2018|access-date=January 6, 2024}} He averaged 23.5 points and 10 rebounds per game as a senior. Ranked the No. 86 prospect in his class by [[Rivals.com]], Baugh committed to play college basketball at [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]].{{cite web|title=Frogs Add Memphis Transfer Baugh|url=https://gofrogs.com/news/2021/4/16/mens-basketball-frogs-add-memphis-transfer-baugh.aspx|work=[[TCU Horned Frogs]]|date=April 16, 2021|access-date=January 6, 2024}} ==College career== As a freshman, Baugh averaged 4.1 points, 3.6 rebounds, and 2.6 assists per game. He averaged 3.4 points, 2.6 rebounds and 1.9 assists per game as a sophomore. Following the season, Baugh transferred to [[TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball|TCU]]. Baugh averaged 10.6 points, 4.5 rebounds, and 4.5 assists per game as a junior. Following the season, he signed with an NBA certified agent, and served a six-game suspension.{{cite news|title=TCU's Damion Baugh serving 6-game ban for signing with agent|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/35028358/tcu-damion-baugh-serving-6-game-ban-signing-agent|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=November 14, 2022|access-date=January 6, 2024}} As a senior, Baugh averaged 12.6 points, 4.7 rebounds, and 5.8 assists per game, helping TCU reach the second round of the NCAA Tournament.{{cite news|title=TCU's Damion Baugh staying in NBA draft while Emanuel Miller returns to Frogs, reports say|url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/tcu-horned-frogs/2023/06/01/tcus-damion-baugh-staying-in-nba-draft-while-emanuel-miller-returns-to-frogs-reports-say/|work=[[The Dallas Morning News]]|date=June 1, 2023|access-date=January 6, 2024}} He was named to the Second Team All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]].{{cite web|title=Phillips 66 All-Big 12 Men's Basketball Awards Announced|url=https://s3.amazonaws.com/big12sports.com/documents/2023/3/5/Men_s_Basketball_All_Big_12_Team_22_23_.pdf|work=[[Big 12 Conference]]|date=March 5, 2023|access-date=January 6, 2024}} ==Professional career== ===South Bay Lakers (2023–2024)=== After going undrafted in the [[2023 NBA draft]], Baugh signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] on September 7, 2023.{{cite web|title=Los Angeles Lakers Sign Four Players|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/los-angeles-lakers-sign-four-players-090723|website=NBA.com|date=September 7, 2023|access-date=January 16, 2024}}{{cite news|first=Davis|last=Wilson|title=Basketball: Damion Baugh Signs with the Los Angeles Lakers|url=https://www.si.com/college/tcu/frogs-in-the-pros/basketball-damion-baugh-signs-with-the-los-angeles-lakers|work=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=June 26, 2023|access-date=January 6, 2024}} However, he was waived on October 16{{cite web|title=Los Angeles Lakers Waive Three Players|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/lakers-waive-three-players-10-16-23|website=NBA.com|date=October 16, 2023|access-date=January 16, 2024}} and twelve days later, he joined the [[South Bay Lakers]].{{cite web|title=South Bay Lakers Finalize Training Camp Roster and Schedule|url=https://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-lakers-finalize-2324-training-camp-roster-and-schedule|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2023|access-date=January 16, 2024}} ===Westchester Knicks (2024–2025)=== On October 2, 2024, Baugh signed with the [[New York Knicks]],{{cite tweet|author=NY_KnicksPR|title=.@nyknicks Sign Damion Baugh to Exhibit 10 Contract|number=1841599096550756527|user=NY_KnicksPR|date=October 2, 2024|access-date=October 3, 2024}} but was waived on October 9.{{cite tweet|author=NY_KnicksPR|title=.@nyknicks Waive Damion Baugh and Alex O’Connell|number=1844023736347111572|user=NY_KnicksPR|date=October 9, 2024|access-date=October 9, 2024}} On October 28, he joined the [[Westchester Knicks]].{{cite web|title=Westchester Knicks Announce 2024-25 NBA G League Training Camp Roster|url=https://westchester.gleague.nba.com/news/westchester-knicks-announce-2024-25-nba-g-league-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=November 1, 2024}} ===Charlotte Hornets (2025)=== On February 12, 2025, Baugh signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite web|title=Charlotte Hornets Sign Damion Baugh To Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/charlotte-hornets-sign-damion-baugh-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=February 12, 2025|access-date=February 12, 2025}} He made his NBA debut that day, logging 16 points, 5 rebounds, and 3 assists off the bench in a 102–86 loss to the [[2024–25 Orlando Magic season|Orlando Magic]].{{cite web | last=Dow | first=Lawrence | title=Damion Baugh excels in debut with Charlotte Hornets, joins other TCU Horned Frogs in NBA | website=Fort Worth Star-Telegram | date=2025-02-13 | url=https://www.star-telegram.com/sports/college/big-12/texas-christian-university/article300256404.html | access-date=2025-12-05}} Baugh made 15 appearances for Charlotte during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 7.3 points, 3.3 rebounds, and 3.7 assists. ===Valley Suns (2025–2026)=== On September 19, 2025, Baugh officially signed with the [[Phoenix Suns]] on an [[Exhibit 10]] training camp contract.{{Cite web|title=Suns' Damion Baugh: Lands with Phoenix|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/suns-damion-baugh-lands-with-phoenix/|access-date=October 21, 2025|website=cbssports.com|language=en}} He was waived by the Suns on October 15.{{Cite web|title=Suns' Damion Baugh: Waived by Phoenix|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/suns-damion-baugh-waived-by-phoenix/|access-date=October 21, 2025|website=cbssports.com|language=en}} On November 7, Baugh was named to the [[Valley Suns]] opening night roster.{{cite web|url=https://valley.gleague.nba.com/news/valley-suns-announce-2025-26-opening-night-roster|title=VALLEY SUNS ANNOUNCE 2025-26 OPENING NIGHT ROSTER|website=gleague.nba.com|date=November 7, 2025|access-date=November 7, 2025}} === Al Ahly Ly (2026) === Baugh joined Libyan champions [[Al Ahly Ly (basketball)|Al Ahly Ly]] for the [[Basketball Africa League]] (BAL). On April 1, 2026, he set a new [[List of BAL records|all-time record]] for most assists in a game, when he dished out 18 assists in a 118–97 win over [[Dar City BC|Dar City]].{{Cite web |title=First records fall in the 2026 BAL season |url=http://bal.nba.com/news/first-records-fall-in-the-2026-bal-season |access-date=2026-04-05 |website=The BAL |language=en}} === Calgary Surge (2026) === In June 2026, Baugh signed with the [[Calgary Surge]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]] (CEBL).{{cite news |last1=Brayshaw |first1=Kaiden |title=Calgary Surge secures its first win with 102-99
